questions.question: A solid wooden block has 5 flat faces in total. Two of the faces are identical triangles that sit at opposite ends and are parallel to each other, and the other 3 faces are rectangles that join those two triangles. What is the name of this solid?
questions.explain: Step 1: it has two identical parallel faces, so it is a prism. Step 2: a prism is named by the shape of those bases, and here they are triangles, so it is a triangular prism. The common trap is naming it after a side face and calling it a rectangular prism.

questions.question: A solid glass paperweight has 5 flat faces in total. One face is a square that it rests on, and the other 4 faces are triangles that all meet at one single point at the top. What is the name of this solid?
questions.explain: Step 1: the triangular faces meet at one apex, so it is a pyramid. Step 2: name a pyramid by its base, and the base here is a square, so it is a square pyramid. The trap is naming it after the slanted triangle faces and saying triangular pyramid.

questions.question: A solid metal bar has 8 flat faces in total. Two of the faces are identical six-sided shapes at the two ends and are parallel to each other, and the other 6 faces are rectangles joining them. What is the name of this solid?
questions.explain: Two identical parallel faces means prism, and those bases have 6 sides, so it is a hexagonal prism. Two traps to avoid: naming it after the rectangular sides, and using the total of 8 faces instead of the 6 sides of the base.

questions.question: A solid clay model has 6 flat faces in total. One face is a five-sided shape that the model stands on, and the other 5 faces are triangles that all meet at one point on top. What is the name of this solid?
questions.explain: Faces meeting at one apex means pyramid, and the base is a pentagon (5 sides), so it is a pentagonal pyramid. The trap is naming it triangular pyramid because the slanted faces you see are triangles — the base decides the name.

questions.question: A prism has 8 faces altogether. Six of them are rectangles, and the other two are identical and parallel to each other. What is the name of this prism?
questions.explain: The 6 rectangles are the side faces, so the two leftover identical parallel faces are the bases, and they must each have 6 sides — a hexagonal prism. Do not use the total number of faces (8) or the shape of the side faces to name it.

questions.question: A pyramid has 6 faces altogether. Five of them are triangles that meet at one apex, and one is the base. What is the name of this pyramid?
questions.explain: Each triangular face sits on one edge of the base, so 5 triangles means the base has 5 sides: a pentagonal pyramid. The traps are naming it after the triangle faces, or using the total of 6 faces to say hexagonal.

questions.question: Maya sets up her tent at Cultus Lake. The tent has two identical triangle-shaped ends that face each other, a rectangular floor, and two slanted rectangular walls. What is the name of the solid shape of Maya's tent?
questions.explain: The two identical parallel triangle ends are the bases, so the tent is a triangular prism. Many students see the big rectangular floor and walls and answer rectangular prism, but side faces never give the name.

questions.question: Devon has a solid from the classroom shape kit and wants to name it correctly. Which step should he do FIRST?
options: Find the largest rectangular side face and name the solid after that shape
Measure the height of the solid from the table to the top
Count how many faces the solid has in total and use that number as the name
Find the two identical parallel faces (or the single face opposite the apex) and name the solid after that shape
questions.explain: The naming rule is always: locate the base first (two identical parallel faces for a prism, the face opposite the apex for a pyramid), then use the base's shape in the name. Starting from the biggest side face or the total face count leads to wrong names like calling a triangular prism a rectangular prism.

questions.question: A chocolate box at a Vancouver gift shop has two identical parallel triangle ends and three rectangular sides. Ben says it is a rectangular prism because three of its five faces are rectangles. Which statement is correct?
options: Ben is wrong: the two identical parallel faces are triangles, so it is a triangular prism
Ben is right: a solid is named after the face shape that appears most often
Ben is wrong: it is a triangular pyramid because it has triangles
Ben is right, because the rectangular faces are the largest faces on the box
questions.explain: A prism is named by its bases — the two identical parallel faces — not by the side faces or by which face shape appears most often, so this box is a triangular prism. It is not a pyramid because there is no single apex where faces meet.

questions.question: A display case at a science centre holds a solid with 5 flat faces. Four of the faces are triangles that all meet at one point at the top, and the fifth face is a quadrilateral measuring 30 cm by 20 cm that the solid rests on. What is the correct name of this solid?
questions.explain: Step 1: faces meeting at one apex means it is a pyramid, not a prism. Step 2: the base is a 30 cm by 20 cm rectangle, so it is a rectangular pyramid. The usual mistake is calling it a triangular pyramid because the four slanted faces are triangles.

questions.question: A totem-shaped display column at a Kelowna museum has 7 faces: two identical parallel five-sided faces at the top and bottom, and 5 rectangles around the sides. Priya calls it a rectangular prism because every side face she can touch is a rectangle. Which statement corrects her best?
options: She is right, since the rectangles are the faces you actually see
It is a pentagonal pyramid, because five-sided shapes make pyramids
It is a pentagonal prism, because the two identical parallel bases are pentagons
It should be called a rectangular prism because 5 of its 7 faces are rectangles
questions.explain: Every prism has rectangles around its sides, so rectangles can never decide the name — the two identical parallel bases do, and here they are pentagons. It is also not a pyramid, since a pyramid has only one base and one apex.

questions.question: A bakery in Richmond builds a two-part cake. The bottom part has two identical parallel six-sided faces (top and bottom) joined by 6 rectangles. The part sitting on top has a square bottom and 4 triangular faces that meet at one point. What are the correct names of the two parts?
questions.explain: Name each part by its base: the bottom has hexagon bases and rectangular sides, so it is a hexagonal prism, and the top has a square base with faces meeting at an apex, so it is a square pyramid. The trap is naming either part after its side faces, which gives wrong answers like rectangular prism or triangular pyramid.
